current.text: He is a rookie and the number one overall pick. Washington is building around him as its centerpiece.
He is projected to start at small forward next to Trae Young, Kyshawn George, Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr. Depending on the lineup, he may also play shooting guard or power forward.

Experts agree that Trae Young and Anthony Davis will take a lot of usage and get the preferred touches. That caps his shots in year one, and the 35% usage he had in summer league will be hard to repeat.
Washington may bring him along slowly. He could play around 28 minutes a night early in the season instead of 34 or more.

Experts agree he is overdrafted at a Yahoo ADP in the 70s. They project him around or outside the top 100 in category leagues. One projects him about 180th, and another says his best case does not reach the top 100. One expert calls him fine around pick 120 and too high at 85 on ESPN.
He had 5 steals and 3 blocks in two summer league games, which is not usual for him. If those defensive stats stick, his value rises.
The Wizards ended their rebuild and are trying to compete for the play-in. Late-season resting and minutes cuts from past years should not be a concern.

durable.text: He is a high-usage volume scorer with shot creation and a good handle. He gets to the rim and the free throw line at will. In summer league he shot 89% at the rim and took about 7 free throws per game, which matched his rate at BYU.

His shooting is a weakness. He has low three-point volume, a below average free throw percentage and questionable shot selection. In summer league he shot 39% from the field and went 1 for 11 from three.
Experts rate his defense, steals and blocks as poor. His rebounds are okay but not strong.
Experts disagree on his passing. Some call his assists very good and praise his pick and roll play for his size. Others call his passing unclear or not strong.
Turnovers are his weakest projected category, at about 2.3 per game. Points are his only clear strength.
Experts consider his profile the worst for category leagues among the top four rookies. He is worth clearly more in points leagues.

note: The sites rank him 85 to 92 and value him at 4 to 6 USD. That puts him inside our 144-player draft, but experts think a line built around about 18.7 points with weak shooting and many turnovers plays outside the top 100 in categories. Only bid a few USD as a late flyer, mainly on punt TO teams that need points, and let others pay for the No. 1 pick hype. Early in the season, check his minutes (28 or 34), his FG% and three-point volume, and whether his summer league steals and blocks hold up.
